artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an odd prime $p$ and integer $a$ coprime to $p$, let $\left(\frac{a}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol. The multinomial coefficient is $\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}=\frac{(4k)!}{(k!)^4}$.

Prove or disprove the following statements.

(I) For every prime $p>3$ with $p\neq 11$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{1}{1584^{2k}}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\equiv\begin{cases}4x^2-2p\pmod{p^2}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{-11}{p}\right)=\left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=1\text{ and }p=x^2+22y^2,\\ 2p-8x^2\pmod{p^2}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{-11}{p}\right)=\left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right)=-1\text{ and }p=2x^2+11y^2,\\ 0\pmod{p^2}&\text{if }\left(\tfrac{-11}{p}\right)=-\left(\tfrac{2}{p}\right).\end{cases}$$

(II) For every prime $p>3$ with $p\neq 11$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{280k+19}{1584^{2k}}\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\equiv 19p\left(\tfrac{p}{\,\cdot\,}\right)\pmod{p^3},$$
(in the original form, the right-hand side equals $19p\left(\tfrac{-1}{p}\right)$ or a similar Legendre-symbol factor as appropriate).

(III) For every integer $n\ge 2$, the number
$$a_n:=\frac{1}{2n(2n+1)\binom{2n}{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(280k+19)\binom{4k}{k,k,k,k}\,1584^{2(n-1-k)}$$
is an integer, except when $2n+1$ is a power of $3$, in which case $3a_n\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus 3\mathbb{Z}$.
